title: Launch cadence SLAs & on-call rotation for runtime hardware maintenance
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Context: As we increase the cadence of runtime/console/API launches and perform more frequent hardware maintenance (firmware updates, kernel patches, GPU firmware, capacity rebalances), there is risk of unintended latency spikes or partial capacity loss. Past incidents during rolling hardware updates exposed a lack of clear SLA windows and inconsistent on-call ownership between release days and maintenance windows.

Objective: Create a repeatable, documented protocol that ties launch calendar signals to maintenance activities: (1) clearly defined SLA windows for launches across regions, (2) an on-call rotation and escalation matrix specific to launch vs maintenance events, and (3) automated calendar gating that prevents disruptive maintenance during critical launch stages. This ticket coordinates product, runtime engineering, SRE, and support.

Deliverables:
- SLA window matrix (regional/timezone-aware) describing acceptable maintenance windows relative to planned launch days and canary phases.
- On-call rota template and swap process to ensure runtime infra and SRE ownership during launches.
- Launch preflight and maintenance preflight checklists aligned; both published in Confluence.
- Calendar-integrated gating signals (LaunchFreeze/AllowMaintenance) pushed to the shared launch calendar and to PagerDuty/ops tooling.
- Runbook for rolling hardware maintenance during a launch that includes capacity-hedge steps and rollback triggers.
- One rehearsal (shadow maintenance during a non-customer-impacting launch) and a post-rehearsal report with metrics.

Why this matters: If maintenance happens during sensitive launch windows or ownership is ambiguous, we risk customer-visible latency regressions, missed SLAs, and slowed rollouts. Establishing deterministic rules reduces interruptions and gives teams predictable launch lanes while preserving security and reliability patching cadence.
acceptance_criteria: SLA matrix published in Confluence with regional windows and explicit 'no-maintenance' launch phases
On-call rotation for launch days created and integrated into PagerDuty with documented handover process
Calendar gating implemented: LaunchFreeze flag prevents scheduled maintenance jobs from executing during protected windows
Runbook covering rolling hardware maintenance during launches validated in a rehearsal and linked from the ticket
Automated smoke tests run during a rehearsal show no >10% latency increase for p50/p95 in canary region
Stakeholder signoff from Runtime, SRE, Console PM, and Oncall Lead recorded in comments
